Breadcrumb

Where a page sits, root first, and the dark strip that carries the same trail above the footer with a way back to the top. The last crumb is the page you are on and never links.

2 variantsLandmarkToken-driven

Preview

The trail on a page. Hover the first crumb: it goes from link blue to pink, with no underline.
  1. Iron Software
  2. Suite

Footer strip

variant="footer": the full-width band between a page and its footer, 80 tall. Its content stops at the 1232 column the 1440 frame draws, so on a wider screen the trail and the link stay where they are at 1440. “Back to top” goes to #top, which every browser reads as the top of the document.
  1. Iron Software
  2. Suite
Back to top

Trails

A root page has a one-crumb trail, and it is still a trail: every page announces the same shape. A crumb before the last with no href is a section with no page of its own, so it takes the body colour, not the link’s.

Code

          
<Breadcrumb
  variant="footer"
  items={[
    { label: 'Iron Software', href: '/' },
    { label: 'Suite' },
  ]}
/>

Guidelines

✓ Do
  • End the trail with the page you are on, with no href: it is aria-current="page" and never links.
  • Use the footer strip once, directly above the site footer, on a page long enough to need “Back to top”.
  • Change label on a page with a second trail, so the two landmarks have different names.
✗ Don't
  • Don't type the separator into a label. It is drawn by CSS so a screen reader reads crumbs, not “slash”.
  • Don't use the trail as the page's main navigation; it says where a page is, not where else to go.
  • Don't put the default trail on a dark band — use footer, whose colours are fixed for one.
